claims.claim_text: Government FX interventions and central bank rate hikes cannot address structural eurodollar dollar-demand shortages, making policy tools ineffective and any currency stabilization temporary.
reasoning_chain: Step 1: Japan deployed all standard tools — rate hikes to 30-year highs, record FX intervention (72.5B USD equivalent), official warnings and US coordination language.
Step 2: Each intervention produced short-term stabilization (hours to weeks) but the yen resumed its decline because none of these actions altered global dollar supply or recirculation.
Step 3: When Japan intervened, it sold US Treasuries to get dollars — mechanically drawing on reserves, not creating new dollar supply.
Step 4: The structural cause (dollar demand from energy imports, eurodollar funding gaps, China spillover) remained unchanged after each policy action.
Step 5: This demonstrates central bank impotence in eurodollar-driven crises — markets respond to balance sheet realities, not policy announcements.
